page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. The shared CPU allocation impacts raw compute throughput, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance ranking in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. However, Geekbench single-core scores are strong, placing in the top 25%, while Geekbench multi-core and software compilation metrics sit in the average range. Memory performance shows a similar divergence: small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 411.75 GB/sec, but large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. Tradeoffs include weak database operations and static web serving throughput, alongside lower Redis SET performance. Consequently, this configuration is best suited for memory-heavy caching layers, text processing, or lightweight application hosting where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed.
